<explanation>
Based on the file tree and README, WhisperLiveKit is a Python-based library and server that offers real-time, fully local speech-to-text transcription with integrated speaker diarization. It leverages FastAPI with WebSocket support and integrates various backends (including specialized ones for Apple Silicon) to handle Whisper ASR processing along with additional enhancements, such as buffering preview and confidence validation. The project's primary purpose is to provide a local, low-latency solution for live transcription directly from the browser with support for multiple users and real-time speaker identification.

Below is a step-by-step guide to drawing an accurate system design diagram tailored to this project:

1. Identify Main Components:
   • Client Side (Browser Interface):
     - Built-in web UI served through a simple HTML page (found under whisperlivekit/web/live_transcription.html) using MediaRecorder for capturing audio.
     - Sends audio chunks (in webm/opus format) over WebSocket.

   • Server Side (FastAPI Application):
     - API entry point (e.g., whisper_fastapi_online_server.py and FastAPI routes in your example code).
     - WebSocket endpoint ("/asr") that handles incoming audio from clients.
     - HTTP endpoints for serving the web UI.

   • Audio Processing & Transcription Modules:
     - AudioProcessor (handles decoding, buffering via FFmpeg integration).
     - Whisper streaming logic found in whisperlivekit/whisper_streaming_custom modules for ASR.
     - Basic server and core coordination in whisperlivekit/basic_server.py and whisperlivekit/core.py.
  
   • Speaker Diarization:
     - Dedicated diarization module in whisperlivekit/diarization (using Diart and potentially pyannote models).
     - Processes audio streams for real-time speaker identification.

   • External Dependencies & Services:
     - FFmpeg (for live decoding of audio chunks).
     - External model delivery (via dynamic downloading if not cached locally).
     - Optional third-party libraries like torch, diart, and pyannote.audio for advanced features.

2. Determine Relationships & Data Flow:
   • The Browser (client) captures and sends audio data via WebSocket to the FastAPI backend.
   • The FastAPI server receives audio and passes it to the AudioProcessor.
   • The AudioProcessor invokes the streaming ASR backend (and optionally the diarization backend) for real-time transcription.
   • Processed transcription data is sent back to the client through the WebSocket connection.
   • Configuration and inter-module communication (e.g., buffering management and confidence validation) exist between the audio modules and the main server.

3. Architectural Patterns & Design Principles:
   • Separation of concerns is evident by distinguishing between:
       - Client-side UI (responsible for capturing audio and displaying results)
       - Server-side API & business logic (using FastAPI for WebSocket management and routing)
       - Audio processing and ASR logic (modularized in separate Python modules)
   • Modular design that allows plugging in different Whisper backends and optional diarization.
   • Real-time processing with asynchronous event-driven design (e.g., async functions and WebSocket communication).

4. Relevant Technologies, Frameworks, or Libraries:
   • FastAPI and WebSocket support for server/client communication.
   • FFmpeg for runtime audio decoding.
   • Various Whisper ASR backends (faster-whisper, whisper_timestamped, mlx-whisper, or openai-api) for transcription.
   • Diart (and pyannote.audio) for real-time speaker diarization.
   • Python libraries for async processing, dependency injection, and potentially configuration parsing.

5. Guidelines for Tailoring the Diagram:
   - For this full-stack local transcription solution, draw two primary domains: Client and Server.
      • Client Domain:
           ▪ Browser UI with MediaRecorder.
      • Server Domain:
           ▪ HTTP Server (FastAPI) that handles both web page delivery and WebSocket connections.
           ▪ Under the hood, separate out the Audio Processing Unit (AudioProcessor), ASR backend logic (Whisper Streaming modules), and the Speaker Diarization Module.
   - Clearly mark boundaries between asynchronous communication (WebSockets) versus synchronous module interactions (audio processing and server response aggregation).

6. Instruct to Include in the Diagram:
   • Each major component should have a clear label:
       - "Browser / MediaRecorder (Client)"
       - "FastAPI Server (HTTP & WebSocket Endpoints)"
       - "AudioProcessor Module (FFmpeg Decoding & Buffering)"
       - "Whisper ASR Backend (Streaming Transcription)"
       - "Speaker Diarization Module (Diart/pyannote Integration)"
       - "Configuration & Optional Integrations (VAC, Model Management)"
   • Use directional arrows showing:
       - Audio capture flow: Browser → WebSocket → FastAPI → AudioProcessor.
       - Transcription flow: AudioProcessor → Whisper ASR backend → (optional: Diarization module) → WebSocket → Browser.
   • Consider color-coding the components:
       - UI/Client components (e.g., one color/shape like rounded rectangles).
       - Server-side components (e.g., rectangular boxes).
       - External dependencies or optional integrations could be highlighted using different shapes or colors.
   • Include key annotations where necessary such as “Decoding via FFmpeg”, “Real-time processing with async”, or “Model backend lookup”.

7. Extra Detail:
   • Optionally add mini-diagrams for command-line usage and configuration injection (pertaining to parameters for model, chunk size, and optional features).
   • Emphasize the loosely coupled architecture that allows swapping out the ASR backend and enabling/disabling diarization as needed.

This detailed and segmented system design diagram will help effectively explain how the WhisperLiveKit project components interact, ensuring that all crucial architectural and data flow aspects are clearly documented.
</explanation>
